{"id":187340,"tenderTitle":"M2 PCIE NVME SOLID STATE DRIVES FOR FUTURE MASS STORAGE SOLUTIONS EXPRO+","tenderNumber":"1-13538","tenderDescription":"Objective: To develop a memory array based on M2 PCIe NAND flash memory Solid State Drives modules and characterise the radiation effects and possible mitigation methods at software and hardware levels.Description: High density Mass storage solutions based on NAND flash memory Solid State Drives (SSD) are widely used in data server applications and present a great opportunity for space applications. However, their reliability and their tolerance to radiation-induced effects have not been evaluated so far. M2 PCI ExpressNon-Volatile Memory (NVM) storage drives are now commonly used System on Module (SoM) devices, similar in size to Double Dada Rate (DDR) memory modules used in personal computers, and capable of storing over 1TB of data. These SoMs incorporate advanced Error Detection and Correction (EDAC) systems to manage the frequent occurrence of bad blocks and bits in 3D NAND Flash Memories. These devicescan be used in a Redundant Array of Independent Disks (RAID) due to Peripheral Component Interconnect Express (PCIe) interface. Thecombination of powerful EDAC and the hot redundancy of RAID is beneficial for addressing the anticipated radiation effects and wearout in NAND Flash memories when used in Space. The non-volatile nature of these memories helps preventing data loss during power cycling to recover Single Event Functional Interrupts (SEFI) in the control electronics. Additionally, these storage drives are currently used in high-speed computation nodes where radiation effects caused by neutrons and alpha particles are a concern.
